summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiment results on the recommender LLM. Team discussed INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs: INT8 gives the best memory/throughput improvements but shows small regressions on long-context prompts; FP8 offers a middle ground with less quality loss and good perf. Next steps include a larger 2k-request benchmark, sharing security docs and Dedicated pricing, and scheduling a canary on Dedicated cluster.
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-03 15:00 PST | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Atlas Head of ML), Daniel Ruiz (Atlas Infra), Kayla Morgan (Product), Sam (Data Scientist)

Summary: quick review of latest quantization runs (INT8, FP8) on the recommender model; agree on larger benchmark and next steps.

[00:00] Sophie: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, we're doing the weekly P O C sync for the quant experiments. Marco will run through the numbers and then we'll go over next steps.
[00:18] Marco: cool hi all, I'll share my screen in a sec, give me one second. So we ran three main branches this week: baseline fp16, int8 quant, and fp8 quant with calibration.
[00:33] Priya: quick question are these off-the-shelf quant libs or your internal runtime?
[00:39] Marco: primarily our runtime's quant path, so it's Redwood inference engine quantized kernels plus some open-source calibration. there might be a few differences vs community libs but it's representative.
[00:50] Sam: got it. what about the dataset used for calibration?
[00:53] Marco: same dev set as last time, ~10k utterances from our logs, plus a held-out golden set we use for quality checks.
[01:05] [01:05] Marco: starting with memory: INT8 reduced memory footprint by ~48% on the model weights and KV cache compared to FP16, FP8 reduced by ~30%. that translated to about 1.7-1.9x throughput increase for INT8 and 1.3-1.5x for FP8 under our batching pattern.
[01:25] Daniel: did you mean 1.7 to 1.9x on throughput or on tokens-per-second?
[01:30] Marco: tokens-per-second / throughput. for latency P50 it's similar to baseline, P95 is better for FP8 and INT8 in high-batch scenarios but on single-request low-batch P95 INT8 sometimes regresses about 5-8% on long-context requests.
[01:46] Kayla: long-context meaning > 2k tokens?
[01:49] Marco: yeah, roughly over 2k. we suspect the scaling of attention kernels with quantization noise is the cause; also KV cache quantization needs more careful per-layer scaling.
[02:00] Priya: what about quality? Any measurable regressions on our golden prompts?
[02:04] Marco: we ran the 100-golden prompts. FP8 had a minimal regression — BLEU-ish style metric used for the recommender proto, maybe 0.8-1.2% drop on average, but some prompts with numeric precision or SKU similarity had larger delta around 3-4%. INT8 showed about 2.5-4% average drop and a few outliers at ~7% on tricky ranking prompts.
[02:28] Priya: hmmm that's in line with my fears. 4% might be OK for certain features but for the product ranking we need to be careful.
[02:34] Sophie: yeah we recommend running a production-like eval set; also can do hybrid route where you run hot-path queries on FP16/FP8 and fallback to FP16 for flagged long-context or high-precision prompts.
[02:48] Sam: is there tooling to auto-classify which queries are safe for INT8?
[02:52] Marco: we have heuristics in Redwood Optimize — sequence length thresholds, token entropy heuristics, model confidence proxies — those can be surfaced as routing rules. we can share the config.
[03:04] [03:04] Daniel: curious about calibration stability — do we need to recalibrate often as data drifts?
[03:10] Marco: calibration is fairly stable but if the input distribution shifts (new product types, long-skew usage) re-calibration is recommended; we also support per-deployment calibration checkpoints.
[03:22] Kayla: what's the operational difference to run FP8 vs INT8 on Dedicated? cost delta?
[03:26] Sophie: short answer: INT8 gives best density -> lower per-token cost due to more requests per GPU, FP8 sits in the middle. we'll send updated pricing with projected unit economics for each quant profile.
[03:40] Priya: can you ballpark the cost savings we saw in the pilot?
[03:44] Marco: roughly, INT8 pilot extrapolates to ~35-45% per-token cost reduction vs FP16 on our workload because of higher packing and lower memory pressure; FP8 is around 18-28%. variance depends on batch shapes and sequence length distribution.
[03:58] Sam: any difference in warm-up times or cold-starts because of quant kernels?
[04:03] Marco: negligible for steady-state; cold-start kernel JIT might take a few extra seconds if new kernels load, but we're working on caching strategies to reduce that.
[04:12] [04:12] Priya: earlier you mentioned some outliers — do you have examples?
[04:17] Marco: yes I can share a few transcripts: prompt about price matching where SKU ids were numerically similar, the model mixed up SKU A vs SKU 8 in INT8; FP8 kept them mostly correct. those are edge cases but important for ranking.
[04:34] Sophie: we also recommend running a canary for a subset of traffic and monitoring quality metrics like precision@10, click-through sim, and flagged mismatches.
[04:46] Daniel: network side — if we do Dedicated canary in our VPC will there be special peering needs?
[04:51] Sophie: standard VPC peering or private link works; we'll share the network requirements doc. Daniel, you can provision temporary peering and we'll coordinate.
[04:59] Daniel: yes we'll do that, I'll send the constraints.
[05:02] [05:02] Kayla: what's the timeline if we want to move to Dedicated for the canary?
[05:06] Sophie: we can spin a Dedicated pool for pilot in about 2 weeks once contract and payment are cleared; for a shorter POC we can also use hosted reserved burst.
[05:17] Priya: procurement will need SOC2 evidence and KMS details.
[05:20] Sophie: we'll share SOC2 report and KMS integration notes after the call.
[05:27] Sam: curious whether FP8 tuning knobs were heavy-handed or you did per-layer bit allocation?
[05:32] Marco: per-layer scale adjustments and some mixed precision in attention for sensitive layers. FP8 allowed us to keep more dynamic range where needed; INT8 was more aggressive.
[05:44] [05:44] Marco: quick note on numbers: P95 latency for single-request on INT8 sometimes moved from 220ms to 235ms on long-context cases, meanwhile FP8 was 225ms. but throughput at batch size 8 improved much more for INT8.
[06:05] Kayla: those deltas seem OK if we can route correctly. how hard is routing rules to add?
[06:10] Marco: fairly simple, we can add sequence-length threshold + golden-flag header in your client to bypass quantized variants.
[06:18] [06:18] Sophie: next we wanted to align on the larger 2k-request benchmark to get statistically significant numbers. Marco?
[06:23] Marco: yes I'll run it with mixed real traffic shapes and the golden set overlay, measuring P50/P95, tokens/sec, GPU memory, and quality deltas per prompt. I'll package raw outputs and a summary sheet.
[06:34] Priya: good — include confusion examples for top 10 regressions.
[06:38] Marco: will do.
[06:40] [06:40] Daniel: any infra changes on our side needed beyond peering?
[06:44] Marco: nothing special besides network egress rules; we'll provide a checklist.
[06:48] Kayla: procurement timeline question — Sophie, will the pricing you share include pilot credits?
[06:52] Sophie: yes we'll include pilot credit line items and expected usage for the canary.
[06:56] [06:56] Sophie: quick clarifying question about fallback policy — do you want automatic fallback to FP16 if a request fails quality checks in flight?
[07:03] Priya: ideally yes, but prefer a conservative approach: monitor and then auto-fallback only for high-risk queries.
[07:09] Sam: can we toggle fallback rules without deploy?
[07:12] Marco: yes that's part of routing policies in the console; we can set rules and change them in prod without model redeploy.
[07:18] [07:18] Sophie: ok let's run through the timeline: Marco runs 2k bench by 11/10, Sophie sends pricing and security docs by 11/05, Priya provides golden prompts by 11/06, Daniel to provision peering by 11/12, then schedule canary week of 11/17.
[07:34] Priya: that works.
[07:36] Kayla: one more question — did you compare against any managed endpoints like OpenAI or Vertex for latency/cost?
[07:42] Marco: we did a rough cost parity check; managed endpoints had lower ops overhead but higher unit compute cost for our scale. we'll include the competitor snapshot in the slide deck.
[07:55] [07:55] Sophie: all right any other questions?
[07:58] Priya: nothing else. Thanks everyone.
[08:01] Sophie: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

Notes/Artifacts shared: link: /redwood/pilot/atlas/quant-results-2026-11-03.xlsx (artifact), link: /redwood/security/soc2-summary.pdf (artifact), config snippet: routing rule examples (shared in chat).

[End of transcript — approximate timestamps stop at ~08:01 in the recording, rest of meeting included brief logistics].
